notes: Commands are read as recorded by the coding agent, which caps each at 240 characters, so a check at the end of a long chained command can be missed.
Paths are compared lower-cased, with a backslash read as a forward slash.
Leading environment assignments and runner wrappers such as npx, uv run, python -m and pnpm exec are skipped before a command is matched.

Two runs count as the same check when their command words match: the words before the first flag or path, wrappers dropped, so a narrower run of the same check (pytest tests/a.py after pytest) is the same command.
A failed command that holds a check counts as a failed check, and in a chain such as npm test && git push the exit status cannot say which part failed, so the chain counts as its first check.
git diff --stat, git diff --name-only and git show <rev>:<path> are not read as a diff appearing.

practices.definition: After the last file edit before a git commit, a check ran in the session: tests, a linter, a type check or a build.
Both a source file and a test file were edited in the session.
practices.denominator: Sessions that edited a source file.

practices.definition: A check command (tests, a linter, a type check or a build) failed, files were edited, and then the same check succeeded in the session.
practices.denominator: Sessions where a check command failed.

practices.definition: A planning step came before the first file edit in the session: plan mode, a task list, or writing a plan or spec file.
Before a commit or a pull request, the diff appeared in the session (git diff, git show or gh pr diff), whoever asked for it; the session cannot show whether anyone read it.
practices.denominator: Sessions with a commit or a pull request.

practices.definition: A design document (an ADR, RFC, spec or design file, by path) was written or edited in the session.
A dependency audit or a security scanner ran in the session.
